Request to Join

About Event

Your agent works. Then the process crashes, a tool times out, or a human approval takes longer than expected.
Can it pick up where it left off?
Join HackerSquad and Diamond Sponsor Diagrid at the AWS Builder Loft in San Francisco on December 11 for a full-day hackathon focused on building agents that recover from interruptions and finish what they started.
The challenge: build an agent or workflow, make it durable with Diagrid, then interrupt it mid-run and show us what happens next.
Durable execution lets an application preserve progress and resume after an interruption. You’ll put that idea to work—and put your project to the test.
What you can build
Bring your own use case. Build something practical, experimental, or just fun:
An agent that survives a crash: Interrupt a research assistant or multi-step automation and demonstrate how it resumes.

A workflow that waits for a human: Pause for a review or approval, then continue when the decision arrives.

A team of agents that finishes the job: Coordinate handoffs and show what happens when one part gets interrupted.

A game that remembers: Build a durable dungeon master or another interactive experience that keeps its progress through a restart.

These are starting points. The common thread is using Diagrid for durable execution and demonstrating recovery in your project.
The live recovery demo
Your final demo should tell a clear story:
What did you build? Show the task your agent or workflow is trying to complete.

What went wrong? Kill the process or introduce an interruption.

What happened next? Restart it and show how it recovers, what progress it preserves, and whether any work gets repeated.

Start with a simple kill-and-restart test, or go further with timeouts, rate limits, interrupted handoffs, and chaos testing.
Getting started
Diagrid will provide starter examples and technical mentorship to help you build. We’ll share the recommended setup, supported technology options, and any account requirements before the event.
Explore the Diagrid AI docs and quickstart examples for an early look.
Prize categories and judging details will be announced.
Who should join
AI engineers, backend and platform developers, technical founders, and builders curious about making agents more reliable. You don’t need prior experience with durable execution, but come ready to write code and test your assumptions.
Bring your laptop, an idea, and a willingness to kill what you just built.

About Event

This Diwali, bring AI agents together to collaborate, compete, and build what one agent alone cannot

Watch AI agents hack, trade, design, and build — together. Join us in the heart of Silicon Valley for an exciting agent-to-agent showdown.
This Diwali, we're bringing together San Francisco's sharpest AI minds to build multi-agent systems where AI doesn't just assist, it collaborates.
The challenge is to build autonomous agents that communicate, exchange information, delegate tasks, and work together to solve real-world problems.
To compete, every team must build and integrate their agents using the developer platforms provided by our sponsors — Agent37, Lyzr, AdaL, Finch, and Band.

About Diwali
Diwali, also known as the Festival of Lights, is one of the most celebrated festivals in India. It symbolizes the victory of light over darkness and good over evil. During Diwali, people decorate their homes with colorful lights, candles, and beautiful rangoli designs. Families celebrate by sharing sweets, exchanging gifts, wearing new clothes, and enjoying fireworks. It is a time of happiness, love, hope, and togetherness.

Tracks
🛡️ Security — Attack & Defend
Build AI agents that simulate cyberattacks and defend systems against potential threats in a controlled environment.
Red Agent identifies vulnerabilities, tests system defenses, and exposes security weaknesses. Blue Agent detects threats, analyzes vulnerabilities, and strengthens system security. The Red Agent shares its findings with the Blue Agent, which uses them to detect threats and improve system defenses.
Example: One agent attempts to breach a test application while the other detects the attack and recommends security fixes.
💹 Finance — Analyze & Trade
Build AI agents that research financial markets, identify investment opportunities, and make data-driven trading decisions. Analyst Agent gathers market data, tracks trends, and identifies potential investment opportunities. Trader Agent uses market insights to make decisions and execute simulated trades. The Analyst Agent shares market insights with the Trader Agent, which uses them to make informed trading decisions.
Example: One agent tracks stock trends and identifies opportunities while another executes simulated trades based on its analysis.
🎨 Marketing — Create & Copy
Build AI agents that work together to create complete marketing campaigns with engaging visuals and compelling content. Visual Agent generates campaign images, promotional creatives, and marketing videos. Copy Agent creates matching headlines, captions, ad copy, and social media content. The Visual Agent shares creative concepts with the Copy Agent, which turns them into matching marketing content.
Example: Give the agents a product description and get campaign visuals, social media posts, and matching ad copy.
📊 Research — Data & Build
Build AI agents that collect information, analyze data, and turn research into useful applications.
Data Agent searches the web, gathers live information, and organizes it into structured data. Builder Agent transforms the collected data into websites, dashboards, or interactive applications. The Data Agent passes its findings to the Builder Agent, which uses them to create functional, data-driven products.
Example: One agent collects live industry data while another turns it into an interactive research dashboard.

Your flight is preparing for takeoff. Once the cabin doors close, your connection to the cloud disappears. Before switching to airplane mode, you have one mission: build an AI project that runs entirely on-device.

Will your project survive offline?
Why on-device AI?
Unlike traditional AI applications that depend on cloud servers, on-device AI runs models directly on the user's hardware. That means your product can benefit from:
Low latency ⚡

Greater user privacy 🔒

No server inference costs 💸

Offline functionality 📴

Who this is for
👨‍💻 Developers who want to ship AI features without an inference bill

🤖 ML and AI engineers curious about deploying models beyond the cloud

⚙️ Edge, embedded, and robotics engineers building against real hardware constraints

🚀 Founders and product managers evaluating on-device versus cloud AI

🎓 Students and self-taught builders who want to leave having built something real

Start at zero. Leave with a demo.
Zero to Demo is a free, beginner-friendly Bay Area hackathon where you’ll turn an idea into a working project using AI. First-time builders, creatives, developers, and engineers are all welcome. No prior coding experience is required.
Come solo or bring a team. You’ll experiment with tools, build around an idea that interests you, and share what you made in a demo at the end of the event.
The Schedule:

11:00 AM — kickoff, form teams, and start building.

7:00-8:00 PM — Judging & Finalize awards

What you can build
Choose one of four tracks to give your project a direction:
Automate
Make everyday tasks easier with AI agents, personal assistants, or workflow tools. Build something that handles the work you’d rather not do, such as organizing your schedule or keeping track of follow-ups.
Impact
Build something that addresses a real need in education, accessibility, sustainability, or your community. Think of a problem you’ve experienced or seen firsthand, and create a tool that helps.
Create
Use AI to make something interactive: a game, a storytelling tool, a music project, or another creative experience. This track is for exploring what you can make, not just what you can automate.
Frontier
Experiment with voice agents, robotics, tools that work with images and audio, or new ways to interact with technology. Try an unconventional idea and see how far you can take it.
The demo
Build toward something you can show. A focused project with one working feature is a stronger starting point than a long list of unfinished ones.
Your demo is a chance to explain your idea, show how it works, and share what you learned along the way. Present it well!

UC San Diego's Design and Innovation Building hosts Techstars Startup Weekend San Diego, bringing builders, designers, lawyers, and the legally curious together for a weekend focused squarely on legal tech, software, and innovation. The theme: reimagining law for the AI era. The legal industry touches nearly everyone and has changed less than almost any other sector in the last few decades. This weekend is about building the tools that could finally change that, from AI that helps a tenant fight an eviction to software that lets a small business draft a contract without a $400-an-hour phone call.
Around 100 participants will pitch ideas, form teams around the strongest ones, and spend the weekend building toward a final pitch to a panel of judges. Mentors and coaches work alongside teams throughout, helping them get out of the building to validate ideas with real users, sharpen product direction, and prepare a polished final pitch.
Julian Bryant , Lead Organizer of Techstars Startup Weekend San Diego and an attorney/software developer himself, has facilitated roughly 40 Startup Weekends and brings a track record of real companies launched from the format, including CreativeUp, a Santa Barbara-based company that formed at one of his earliest events and is still operating more than six years later.
Jacques Chirazi , Director of the Basement and Entrepreneurship Center at UC San Diego's Office of Innovation and Commercialization, brings UC San Diego's student entrepreneurship ecosystem into the weekend, connecting participants to campus resources that can carry momentum well past Sunday night.
